title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant (Helpdesk)

Cambridge (Hybrid Working)

£16.38 per hour

Full-Time 36.5 hours per week

Temporary Assignment until March 2027

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an Accounts Assistant to join a busy Finance Division in Cambridge. This role will support a finance helpdesk function, providing first-line support to users of a finance system and associated services. Full training will be provided, making this an excellent opportunity for someone with strong administrative and finance skills looking to develop their experience.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide first-line support to colleagues, customers, and suppliers via phone and email.
- Respond to finance system queries and helpdesk requests.
- Maintain accurate records and assist with finance administration tasks.
- Support users with system navigation and finance-related processes.
- Work collaboratively with colleagues across the organisation to resolve queries efficiently.
- Use Microsoft Excel, Outlook, and Word to manage and process information.

About You

We're looking for someone who:
- Has previous administration or finance administration experience.
- Is confident communicating with a wide range of people both verbally and in writing.
- Has good Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel.
- Possesses strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Enjoys problem-solving and delivering excellent customer service.

What's on Offer?
- Competitive hourly rate of £16.38 per hour.
- Hybrid working, with a mixture of office and home-based working.
- Full training provided.
- Long-term temporary assignment through to March 2027.

title: Accounts Receivable
description:
Cashier Administrator

Location: Peterborough
Salary: Up to £27,000 per annum
Hours: Full-time, 37.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday, 8:30am to 5:00pm (hybrid after 3/6 months)

The Opportunity

We are looking for a highly organised and detail-focused Cashier Administrator to join our busy finance team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone with previous finance or cashiering experience who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment and takes pride in maintaining accuracy.

You will play a key role in ensuring financial transactions are processed efficiently, reconciliations are completed accurately, and finance records are maintained to a high standard.

Key Responsibilities
- Posting and allocating daily cash sheets and banking transactions.
- Processing journals where required.
- Handling finance-related queries and resolving issues promptly.
- Completing full bank reconciliations and investigating discrepancies.
- Auditing cashbook supporting documentation to ensure completeness and authorisation.
- Maintaining accurate filing and record-keeping systems.
- Posting cash-paid transactions, including cheque payments and cleared banking entries.
- Supporting the wider finance team with administrative duties as required.

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous experience within a finance, accounts, cashiering or administrative role.
- Strong attention to detail and high levels of accuracy.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- The ability to manage a high volume of transactions efficiently.
- Good communication skills and a proactive approach to problem-solving.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
- Experience using accounting or finance systems would be advantageous but is not essential.

Benefits
- Competitive salary up to £27,000 depending on experience.
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays.
- Contributory pension scheme.
- Life assurance.
- Ongoing training and development opportunities.
- Career progression within a growing organisation.
- Employee discounts and benefits platform.
- Friendly and supportive team environment.

Please apply for this role and send your CV to . Interviews to be held on site this week.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Robert Half are delighted to be partnering with an established and highly regarded business based in Cambourne, Cambridge, to recruit a Credit Controller to join their finance team.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Credit Controller who enjoys taking ownership of their ledger, building strong relationships with customers and internal stakeholders, and playing a key role in improving cash collection and reducing outstanding debt.

Reporting into the Credit Control Manager, you will take responsibility for a designated portfolio of customers, working closely with operational teams across the business to ensure debts are managed effectively and queries are resolved promptly. The role offers a varied workload within a supportive and collaborative finance environment.

Responsibilities

As the Credit Controller, you will be responsible for:
- Managing and monitoring the collection of outstanding customer balances
- Working towards monthly cash collection targets
- Building effective relationships with customers and internal stakeholders
- Preparing and distributing aged debt reports
- Issuing customer statements and collection correspondence
- Managing accounts that require credit restrictions or "on stop" procedures
- Investigating and resolving queries that may be delaying payment
- Maintaining accurate and up-to-date customer account records
- Processing daily cash receipts, allocations and monthly direct debit payments
- Supporting the setup of new customer accounts
- Supporting the Credit Control Manager with projects aimed at improving cash collection and overall credit control processes

Your Profile

The successful candidate will ideally have:
- Previous experience working within Credit Control
- A proven track record of successfully collecting debt and delivering against targets
- Strong communication and relationship-building skills
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to prioritise a busy workload
- Good knowledge of Excel
- Previous experience using ERP/accounting systems, with IFS experience advantageous
- A proactive, professional and positive approach
- The ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a wider team
- A full UK driving licence

What's on Offer?
- Competitive salary of £30 - £32,000
- Hybrid working (Three days in the office and two from home)
- Opportunity to join an established business
- Varied Credit Control position, with plenty of interaction across the wider organisation.
- Occasional travel to other locations across the UK.

For further information or to apply, please contact Robert Half.

title: Purchase Ledger Clerk
description:
Purchase Ledger Clerk

Department: Finance / Accounts

Location: Peterborough

Salary: £27,000

About the Role

We are looking for a detail-oriented Accounts Payable Clerk to join our finance team. This role is responsible for maintaining accurate purchase ledger records, ensuring invoices and payments are processed efficiently, and supporting the smooth operation of day-to-day finance activities.

The successful candidate will have strong organisational skills, excellent attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining high levels of accuracy.

Key Responsibilities
- Maintain purchase ledger accounts and ensure records are accurate and up to date.
- Review ledgers regularly to minimise aged debt and resolve outstanding account queries.
- Download and allocate bank statements on a daily basis.
- Investigate and resolve cash allocation issues, obtaining remittances and supporting documentation where required.
- Process supplier invoices and credit notes accurately and within agreed timescales.
- Reconcile intercompany invoices and credits.
- Accurately code invoices and credit notes to the correct nominal ledger accounts.
- Complete monthly and ad hoc supplier statement reconciliations.
- Prepare and process payment runs in accordance with company procedures.
- Process ad hoc payment requests and employee expense claims, ensuring all approvals and supporting documentation are in place.
- Assist with month-end processes and reporting requirements.
- Liaise with colleagues and stakeholders to resolve invoice, payment, and account queries.

Skills & Experience
- Previous experience in an Accounts Payable, Purchase Ledger, or Finance Assistant role.
- Accountancy graduates.
- Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Good understanding of accounting processes and financial controls.
- Competent in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
- Ability to manage workload effectively and meet deadlines.
- Experience working with accounting or finance systems is desirable.

Personal Attributes
- Customer-focused approach.
- Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to identify and implement solutions.
- Proactive and organised.
- Team player willing to support colleagues when required.
- Committed to continuous improvement and delivering high standards of work.

Please send your CV to or apply for this role, interviews to be held next week.

title: Purchase Ledger Controller
